title: Blameless Timeline and Evidence Standards for Incident Reviews
author: Asha Raman
content:
Summary:
This page prescribes standardized, blameless requirements for incident timelines and evidence collection for all Redwood production incidents. The goal is to ensure consistent-quality post-incident reviews, preserve high-fidelity artifacts for RCA, and enable repeatable automation.

Scope:
- Applies to all incidents involving production-facing services (hosted API, dedicated model pools, and console).
- Includes incidents that meet the Incident Classification threshold (P1/P2) or that consume >25% of a relevant service's monthly error budget.
- Excludes internal non-production experiments unless they impact customer-facing metrics.

Why a timeline + evidence standard?
- Consistency: reviewers must be able to reconstruct a timeline without ad-hoc requests.
- Speed: clear evidence manifests accelerate RCA and mitigation playbooks.
- Auditability: compliance and enterprise customers require reproducible investigation artifacts.

High-level SLO alignment (examples):
- redwood-api-prod (text-generation): availability SLO = 99.95% monthly; error budget = 0.05%.
- embeddings-service-prod: p99 latency SLO = 600ms; error budget triggers when p99 > 600ms for 6 hours.
- model-routing: request-failure-rate SLO = 0.3% per week.

Incident timeline expectations (blameless):
1) Immediate (0–1h):
   - Create an incident page in Confluence using the incident template. Fill incident-start time, affected services, classification (P1/P2/etc.), and oncall roster.
   - Create/attach an evidence manifest (see below) to the page.
   - Notify SRE oncall and engineering owners via PagerDuty/Slack channel.
2) Short term (1–24h):
   - Document observed symptoms, customer impact (estimate of requests affected, error budget burn percentage), and mitigation steps taken in the incident page.
   - Attach initial logs/trace links and key metric dashboards.
3) Medium term (24–72h):
   - Draft the incident narrative and preliminary timeline (minute-level events where available).
   - Collect and preserve immutable artifacts for final review.
4) Postmortem (72h–7d):
   - Publish a full postmortem with RCA, action items, and acceptance criteria.
   - Assign owners and due dates for every action.
   - If incident impacted enterprise customers, notify Customer Success and Legal; escalate per the enterprise incident runbook.

Evidence manifest (required fields)
- incident_id: Confluence page id (or incident slug)
- incident_start_utc: ISO8601 timestamp
- affected_services: list of service names (e.g., redwood-api-prod, kv-cache, model-worker-gpu)
- observed_metrics: list of metric names and snapshot links (e.g., api.errors.rate -> https://grafana/redwood/api/errors)
- trace_links: list of trace/trace-group URLs (e.g., https://tracing.redwood/trace/abcd1234)
- logs_query: saved query or file (e.g., logging:/projects/redwood/prod/search?q=ERROR%20Rate)
- config_hashes: git commit SHAs or config snapshot links for service(s) involved
- core_dumps/archive: storage path if applicable (e.g., s3://redwood-incidents/2025-02-14/coredump.tgz)
- screenshots/dashboards: image links or attachments
- retained_artifact_ttl: retention window in days (default 365)

(Example manifest JSON fragment — include on incident page):
{
  "incident_id": "inc-2025-02-13-redwood-api-502",
  "incident_start_utc": "2025-02-13T03:42:00Z",
  "affected_services": ["redwood-api-prod", "model-cache"],
  "observed_metrics": ["grafana://dash/redwood/api/errors"],
  "trace_links": ["https://tracing.redwood/trace/abcd1234"],
  "logs_query": "logging:/projects/redwood/prod?q=service:redwood-api AND status>=500"
}

Minimum evidence checklist (attach at time of page creation):
- Snapshot of primary dashboards (PNG or dashboard link).
- At least one high-level trace that crosses the customer request path.
- Representative log slice: 5–10 contiguous minutes that show errors or latency spikes.
- Relevant config version commit SHA(s).
- Screenshot of PagerDuty/alerting trigger with timestamp.
- Error budget burn estimate (percent and absolute units).

Ownership and roles (who does what)
- Incident commander (IC): coordinates response and ensures evidence manifest is updated in 0–1h. Owner: rotating SRE oncall.
- Service owner(s): provide config SHAs and validate the timeline. Owner: service engineering manager.
- Postmortem author: drafts narrative and action items within 72h. Owner: designated author (can be IC or service owner).
- RCA reviewer(s): at least one SRE + one service owner.

Postmortem deliverables and acceptance criteria
- Complete timeline (minute-resolution if available).
- Clear causal chain linking root cause to impact (noting contributing factors).
- Action items with owners, due dates, and a test or validation step.
- Evidence manifest attached and verified (link checks succeed).
- Severity and customer impact stated with mitigation rationale.

Review cadence and meeting agenda
- Within 7 days: run a blameless review meeting (max 60 minutes):
  1) Quick recap and impact (5m)
  2) Timeline walk-through (15m)
  3) Root cause and contributing factors (15m)
  4) Action items and acceptance criteria (15m)
  5) Open questions and follow ups (10m)
- Invitees: SRE oncall, service owner, product representative, security/legal if sensitive.

Retention and compliance
- Default artifact retention = 365 days.
- For incidents involving customer data or regulated workloads, extend retention per legal guidance and mark page confidentiality = restricted.
- Audit snapshot: keep the evidence manifest and references immutable (export to S3/archive bucket) before editing the incident page for legal auditability.

Automation and tooling recommendations
- Incident creation: use the "incident-create" CLI to scaffold the page and evidence manifest. Example:
  curl -X POST https://infra-api.redwood/internal/incidents \
    -H 'Authorization: Bearer $INFRATOKEN' \
    -d '{"service":"redwood-api-prod","start":"2025-02-13T03:42:00Z","classification":"P1"}'
- Logs: prefer saved queries (logging:/...) rather than raw downloads to keep context.
- Traces: create a span-group link and attach to manifest.
- Dashboard snapshots: use grafana API to export PNGs and attach to Confluence page automatically.

Escalation matrix example (error budget driven)
- If incident causes >10% of monthly error budget to burn within 1 hour -> auto-escalate to SRE manager + product owner.
- If incident duration >4 hours and customer impact persists -> signaled page to exec SRE and CS lead.

Quality gates for closure
- All action items have owners and testable acceptance criteria.
- Evidence manifest verified and links reachable.
- CI tests (where applicable) added to prevent recurrence.
- Postmortem annotated with lessons learned and linked to related runbooks or playbooks.

Appendix A — Common queries and snippets
- Grafana snapshot (example):
  curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $GRAFANA_TOKEN" \
       https://grafana.redwood/api/snapshots --data "{\"dashboard\":{...}}"
- Tracing quick link (example): https://tracing.redwood/trace?service=redwood-api&from=2025-02-13T03:30:00Z&to=2025-02-13T04:00:00Z
- Logs example (Stackdriver-like):
  gcloud logging read 'resource.labels.project_id="redwood-prod" AND severity>=ERROR' --start-time="2025-02-13T03:30:00Z" --end-time="2025-02-13T04:00:00Z" > errors.json

Appendix B — Template: quick incident evidence checklist (to paste into incident page)

- incident_start_utc:
- affected_services:
- dashboards_attached:
